Sodalite crystallizes in silica-poor igneous rocks, such as nepheline syenites, formed from alkaline magmas. It is quarried in open pits, selecting the blocks with the most intense and uniform blue color, which are cut and polished for ornamental use and as a semi-precious stone.

Main minerals

Main producing countries

Canada (Ontario, Quebec and British Columbia) and Brazil are the main producers of quality ornamental sodalite.

It is also mined in Russia (Kola Peninsula), Greenland, Namibia and Bolivia.

Strategic applications

  • Construction and infrastructure: wall coverings, countertops and interior decorative elements, often together with lapis lazuli.
  • Jewelry, ornamentation and store of value: intensely blue semiprecious stone, cut into beads, cabochons and figurines; fluorescent specimens attract collectors.

Wollastonite (CaSiO₃)

Extraction

Wollastonite forms when impure limestones react at high temperature with silica supplied by nearby magmatic intrusions, producing skarns (limestones transformed by magma) and other contact metamorphic rocks. It is mined in open pits, and crushed and ground carefully to preserve the elongated shape of its crystals, which makes it valuable as reinforcement in ceramics, plastics and paints.

Main minerals

Main producing countries

China is by far the world's largest producer, followed by India, the United States, Mexico and Finland.

These five countries account for more than 97% of world production.

Strategic applications

  • Energy storage, electric vehicles and mobility: component of brake pads and linings, as a substitute for asbestos.
  • Metallurgical and steel industry: flux in metallurgical processes and thermal insulator, reducing emissions and energy consumption in steelmaking.
  • Chemical industry and catalysis: mineral filler that improves the mechanical and thermal strength of composite materials.
  • Paints, pigments, coatings and lubricants: functional pigment that provides corrosion resistance and pH stability.
  • Glass and ceramics: flux that lowers the firing temperature and improves the strength and dimensional stability of tiles and sanitaryware; this is its main market.

Radioactive minerals

Extraction

Uranium is concentrated mainly in sandstones, where it precipitates from groundwater, and in hydrothermal deposits, such as those of Athabasca (Canada). In sandstones it is extracted by in-situ leaching: a solution is injected into the layer and pumped out loaded with uranium; the rest comes from mines. This produces “yellowcake” (U₃O₈), the basis of nuclear fuel. Thorium comes from monazite in coastal sands.

Main minerals

Main producing countries

Kazakhstan · Canada · Namibia · Australia · Uzbekistan · Russia · Niger · China.

Kazakhstan produces around 40% of the world's uranium, followed by Canada, Namibia and Australia. In Spain, uranium was mined until 2000 at the Saelices el Chico mine (Salamanca).

Strategic applications

  • Nuclear energy: uranium, enriched in its uranium-235 isotope, is the fuel of nuclear power plants, which in Spain generate around one fifth of the electricity.
  • Energy transition / renewable energy: nuclear energy provides stable electricity with very low CO₂ emissions, and thorium is being researched as a fuel for next-generation reactors.
  • Defense and security: enriched uranium powers the reactors of nuclear submarines and aircraft carriers, and depleted uranium is used in armor and armor-piercing projectiles.
  • Medicine and pharmacy: uranium fission in research reactors produces molybdenum-99, from which technetium-99m is obtained, the most widely used radioisotope in diagnostic imaging.

Salts (halite, sylvite, thenardite, trona, glauberite)

Extraction

Salts precipitate when water evaporates from shallow seas and salt lakes in arid climates, forming layers of evaporites. They are worked in underground mines, by dissolving them with water and pumping out the brine, or by solar evaporation in salt pans. Each salt is processed according to its use: sylvite yields potassium chloride for fertilizers; trona, sodium carbonate; and thenardite and glauberite, sodium sulfate.

Main minerals

Main producing countries

China · United States · Canada · India · Russia · Belarus · Germany · Spain · Turkey.

China, the United States and India lead the production of common salt; Canada, Russia and Belarus account for most of the potash; the United States and Turkey dominate natural trona, and Spain is one of the world's main producers of natural sodium sulfate.

Strategic applications

  • Energy storage, electric vehicles and mobility: sodium carbonate is used to precipitate lithium carbonate from brines and is a precursor of the materials for sodium-ion batteries.
  • Energy transition / renewable energy: caverns dissolved out of halite formations allow large-scale storage of hydrogen, natural gas and compressed air.
  • Nuclear energy: salt formations, stable and impermeable, are used as deep geological repositories for radioactive waste.
  • Chemical industry and catalysis: halite is the raw material of the chlor-alkali industry, which produces chlorine, caustic soda and hydrogen, the basis of many chemical processes.
  • Construction and infrastructure: rock salt is the main de-icing agent for keeping roads, bridges and airports free of ice in winter.
  • Agriculture, food security and packaging: sylvite is the main source of potassium for fertilizers, with no substitute, and halite is table salt and a traditional food preservative.
  • Environmental management and water treatment: salt regenerates water softeners and produces the chlorine used to disinfect water, and trona removes acid gases from industrial fumes.
  • Glass and ceramics: sodium carbonate obtained from trona and sodium sulfate from thenardite and glauberite are essential fluxes in glassmaking, including glass for solar panels.

Gypsum (CaSO₄·2H₂O)

Extraction

Gypsum precipitates when the water of seas and lakes evaporates in arid climates, forming evaporite layers, and also forms when anhydrite is hydrated. Spain is one of the largest producers in Europe. It is extracted mainly in open-pit quarries, and the rock is crushed, ground and calcined at low temperature to obtain plaster of Paris and building plaster.

Main minerals

Main producing countries

China is by far the world's largest producer, followed by Iran, Thailand, the United States and Turkey.

Spain is the leading European producer.

Strategic applications

  • Medicine and pharmacy: plaster of Paris is used in orthopedic casts to immobilize fractures and in dental molds and models.
  • Construction and infrastructure: plasterboard for partitions and ceilings, fire-resistant, and setting regulator for Portland cement.
  • Agriculture, food security and packaging: soil amendment that supplies calcium and sulfur and reclaims saline soils; in food, a coagulant for tofu and an additive for doughs and beer.
  • Jewelry, ornamentation and store of value: the fine-grained variety, alabaster, has been used in ornamental sculpture since Antiquity.
